`decision-config-vs-run-split` keeps the configured shape of a workflow separate from any one person's progress through it, so the same workflow can be run by many people at once without their state colliding. `decision-engine-session-scope` ties one engine session to a whole step attempt instead of to each message, matching the brief's description of feedback landing on an already-running process. `decision-gate-representation` records gate-readiness and output-readiness as two plain facts instead of one blurred flag or an invented catalog of individual gates. `decision-exclude-repo-browsing` leaves the repository tree and file-reference picker out of this model because finishing a workflow while watching its output never actually depends on them. `decision-runtime-granularity` is left pending: it treats plan-tool roadmap and plan-tool as separate runtimes for handoff-checking purposes, but the brief never says whether two steps that both happen to run "plan-tool" should count as the same runtime or not, so this needs a person to confirm it. `decision-isolation-boundary` keeps the credential boundary as a rule on the engine session rather than standing up a separate infrastructure entity for it, since hosting shape is not something this domain needs to reason about.
